report.answer_text:
A typical horizontal-jib tower crane moves a load in three ways: the hoist raises and lowers it, the trolley moves it closer to or farther from the tower, and the slewing unit swings it around the tower. (highworks.co.kr)
| Part | What it does |
|---|---|
| Base and foundation | Support the crane and transfer its forces into the ground. On a fixed-base crane, anchors secure the base to the foundation. (morrow.com) |
| Mast (tower) | The vertical steel structure that gives the crane its height and supports the upper assembly. (morrow.com) |
| Slewing unit (turntable) | Uses a large bearing and drive system to rotate the upper assembly around the mast. (morrow.com) |
| Jib (working arm) | The long arm that provides reach and supports the trolley. (morrow.com) |
| Trolley | Travels along the horizontal jib to position the hook closer to or farther from the mast. (highworks.co.kr) |
| Hoist winch and rope | The winch winds or pays out the rope to raise or lower the hook and load. (morrow.com) |
| Hook block | The hook-and-pulley assembly suspended from the hoist rope. The hook connects to the load’s lifting gear. (morrow.com) |
| Counter-jib and counterweights | The shorter rear arm carries counterweights that help offset the overturning effect of the working jib and its load. It may also carry machinery. (morrow.com) |
| Operator’s cab and controls | Let the operator control lifting, trolley travel, and rotation. (morrow.com) |
| Climbing frame and tie-ins, where fitted | The climbing system lets the crane gain height as construction progresses; tie-ins brace the mast against the building. (morrow.com) |
A luffing-jib crane changes its reach by raising or lowering the angle of the jib rather than by moving a trolley along a fixed horizontal arm. (liebherr.com)
